assessments.title: Frontend Architecture & React Patterns
assessments.description: Test your knowledge of state management, component lifecycles, and performance optimization in React 18+.

questions.question: When would using `useCallback` be actively detrimental to performance in React?
options: When passed to an HTML button element with an inline handler
When passed to a memoized child component (React.memo)
When wrapping every function without passing to optimized children, adding unnecessary closure overhead
When used inside a Custom Hook
questions.explanation: useCallback has non-zero memory and compute overhead. If the child component is not wrapped in React.memo or the function isn't a dependency of an effect, useCallback costs more than re-creating a lightweight function.

questions.question: How does React 18 Concurrent Mode handle high-priority UI updates vs background renders?
options: Via `useTransition` and `useDeferredValue` which yield to the main thread during heavy rendering
By pausing JavaScript event loops completely
By server-side rendering all components immediately
questions.explanation: Concurrent React introduces interruptible rendering with useTransition and useDeferredValue, prioritizing urgent user inputs over non-urgent UI transitions.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Zustand over traditional Redux without toolkit?
options: Zustand eliminates boilerplate, avoids Context provider wrappers, and allows transient updates without re-renders
Zustand does not support async actions
questions.explanation: Zustand uses a hook-based pub/sub model with zero provider boilerplate, supports fine-grained selector subscriptions, and handles async cleanly.

questions.question: What does TypeScript `ReturnType<T>` utility type do?
options: Returns the number of arguments in function T
Constructs a type consisting of the return type of function T
Executes function T at compile time
questions.explanation: ReturnType<T> extracts the returned type of a function signature using type inference with `infer`.

questions.question: Why should keys in React lists never be assigned as `Math.random()` or array index when items reorder?
options: Because React throws a syntax error
Because index keys cause DOM reconciliation bugs and random keys cause total DOM unmounting/remounting on every render
Because Tailwind CSS cannot style elements with random keys
Because keys are sent to the backend server
questions.explanation: React relies on stable keys for diffing. Random keys destroy component state on each render, and indices cause state to be bound to the wrong items during insertions/deletions.

assessments.title: RESTful API Design & HTTP Protocols
assessments.description: Evaluate your understanding of HTTP methods, idempotency, status codes, and clean REST endpoint architecture.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is defined as NOT idempotent?
questions.explanation: POST is not idempotent because repeating the identical request typically creates duplicate resources, whereas PUT and DELETE have idempotent side-effects.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate HTTP status code when a client requests a resource that exists but they lack permissions?
questions.explanation: 401 means unauthenticated (who are you?), while 403 Forbidden means authenticated but insufficient authorization (you are not allowed).

questions.question: What header is used in CORS preflight checks to declare allowed custom headers?
questions.explanation: Access-Control-Allow-Headers specifies which HTTP headers can be used during the actual request.

questions.question: What is the recommended payload format for partial updates in RESTful services?
options: HTTP PATCH with JSON Merge Patch or JSON Patch
questions.explanation: HTTP PATCH is designed specifically for applying partial modifications to a resource.
